t.1.58.1: Janamejaya said: Those who have been named here, O brahmin, and those others who have not been named, I wish to hear of them fully, and of other kings of great splendor as well.
t.1.58.2: O greatly fortunate one, you should properly tell me the purpose for which these godlike great chariot-warriors were born here on earth.
t.1.58.3: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: This, O king, is indeed a secret of the gods, so we have heard. Yet I shall tell it to you, having first paid homage to Svayaṃbhū, the Self-Existent.
t.1.58.4: Long ago, having rid the earth of Kṣatriyas three times seven times, Jāmadagnya practised austerities on Mahendra, the finest of mountains.
t.1.58.5: Then, O king, when the world had been made empty of kṣatriyas by the Bhārgava, the kṣatriya women, desiring offspring, approached the brāhmaṇas.
t.1.58.6: Brāhmaṇas of rigorous vows united with them in each fertile season, O tiger among men, not out of lust, nor likewise outside the proper season.
t.1.58.7: From them those kṣatriya women conceived by the thousands, and then, O king, they bore kṣatriyas esteemed for their valor, boys and girls, so that the kṣatriya order might flourish once more.
t.1.58.9: They approached a woman in her season, not out of lust, nor outside her season; likewise the other beings too, even those born of animal wombs, went to their mates only in their season at that time, O bull of the Bharatas.
t.1.58.8: Thus that warrior class, born in kṣatriya women of ascetic brāhmaṇas, prospered through dharma and was endowed with very long life. Then all four classes came to have the brāhmaṇas foremost among them.
t.1.58.10: Then, O protector of the earth, those creatures grew and flourished through dharma, living for a hundred thousand years and devoted to dharma and their vows; and men were wholly freed from sorrows of the mind and from diseases of the body.
t.1.58.11: Then the kṣatra once more ruled over this earth, bordered by the ocean, traversed throughout by lordly elephants, together with its mountains, woods and forests.
t.1.58.13: Casting off the faults that arise from desire and anger, the lords of men protected their subjects, administering punishment righteously to those who deserved punishment.
t.1.58.12: When the kṣatra once again ruled this earth in accordance with dharma, the varṇas, beginning with the brāhmaṇas, then attained the highest joy.
t.1.58.14: So too, while the kṣatra was devoted to dharma, the thousand-eyed Śatakratu rained sweetly, in the right place and at the right time, nourishing the creatures.
t.1.58.15: In those days, O lord of men, no one died while still a child, nor did any man know a woman before he had reached youth.
t.1.58.16: Thus, O bull among the Bharatas, this earth, bounded by the ocean, was filled with long-lived creatures.
t.1.58.17: The kṣatriyas performed great sacrifices with abundant sacrificial fees, and the brahmins then studied the Vedas together with their auxiliary sciences and the Upaniṣads.
t.1.58.18: And at that time, O king, the brāhmaṇas did not sell the Veda, nor did they recite the Vedas in the presence of śūdras.
t.1.58.19: Likewise the vaiśyas here on earth, though they had the fields ploughed with oxen, did not yoke a cow to the pole, and they kept alive even the lean-limbed ones.
t.1.58.21: And, O tiger among men, people devoted to dharma, looking to dharma alone, performed deeds that were in accordance with dharma.
t.1.58.20: Likewise, men did not milk at the expense of calves still living on milk froth, and merchants in those days did not sell their wares with false measures.
t.1.58.22: And all the varṇas were devoted to their own duties, O lord of men; thus at that time, O tiger among men, dharma did not decline anywhere.
t.1.58.24: Thus, O king, while the Kṛta age was then proceeding rightly, the whole earth was abundantly filled with many living creatures.
t.1.58.25: Then, when the world of men had risen to prosperity, O bull of the Bharatas, the Asuras were born in the wombs of the wives of kings, O foremost of men.
t.1.58.23: Cows give birth at the proper time, and so do women, O bull of the Bharatas; and in their seasons the trees bear, both flowers and fruits.
t.1.58.26: For at that time the Daityas, defeated many times in battle by the Ādityas and also cast down from their sovereignty, took birth here on earth.
t.1.58.27: Here on earth, O lord, the proud-minded Asuras, desiring godhood, were born among men and among all sorts of beings, in this one and in that.
t.1.58.28: Among cows and horses, O lord of kings, among donkeys, camels and buffaloes, among flesh-eating creatures, and among elephants and deer.
t.1.58.30: Then certain sons of Diti and of Danu, endowed with strength, having fallen from that world, were born here as kings.
t.1.58.29: O protector of the earth, burdened by those who had been born here and by those still being born, this earth, the upholder of all, was unable to bear herself by her own strength.
t.1.58.32: They oppressed brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras too, and with their might they tormented other creatures as well.
t.1.58.31: Mighty and arrogant, assuming many different forms, those crushers of foes would roam all over this earth bounded by the ocean.
t.1.58.33: Terrifying and slaughtering those various hosts of creatures, they roamed the earth on every side, O king, by hundreds of thousands.
t.1.58.34: Here and there they assaulted the great seers dwelling in their hermitages, hostile to brahmins, drunk with pride in their valor and intoxicated by the strength of their arrogance.
t.1.58.35: Thus oppressed by those great Asuras, swollen with pride in their valor and strength, this Earth, O lord of the earth, approached Brahmā.
t.1.58.36: For then, O king, neither the wind, nor the serpents, nor the mountains were able to bear this earth, overrun by force by the Dānavas.
t.1.58.37: Then, O protector of the earth, the Earth, distressed by her burden and tormented by fear, went for refuge to the god who is the Grandfather of all beings.
t.1.58.38: She beheld the god Brahmā, the imperishable maker of the worlds, surrounded by illustrious gods, twice-born ones, and great seers.
t.1.58.39: Approaching him as he was being praised by joyful gandharvas and apsarases intent on the office of bards, she bowed to him in reverence.
t.1.58.40: Then the Earth, seeking refuge, made her plea to him in the presence of all the guardians of the worlds, O Bhārata.
t.1.58.41: O king, that purpose of Bhūmi had been known from the very first to him, the Self-born Parameṣṭhin, whose self is the primal source of all.
t.1.58.42: For he is the creator of the world. How, O Bhārata, could he not fully understand what lies in the minds of the gods, the asuras, and all the worlds?
t.1.58.44: O Vasuṃdharā, for the purpose for which you have come into my presence, for that very purpose I shall engage all the dwellers of heaven.
t.1.58.43: O great king, the mighty lord of the earth, the source of all beings, the sovereign Śambhu Prajāpati, spoke this to Bhūmi.
t.1.58.45: Having spoken thus and dismissed the Earth, O king, the god Brahmā, creator of beings, then himself commanded all the gods.
t.1.58.46: "To remove the burden of this earth, be born upon this very earth, each of you separately with your portions, to oppose them," so too he said.
t.1.58.47: And in the same way, having gathered together the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases, the Blessed One spoke these excellent words to them all: "Be born with your own portions among humans, as you wish."
t.1.58.48: Then Śakra and all the others, having heard from the preceptor of the gods his words, true, meaningful and wholesome, accepted them at that time.
t.1.58.49: Then they, all of them having resolved to go down to the earth with their own portions, approached Nārāyaṇa, the slayer of enemies, Vaikuṇṭha.
t.1.58.51: For the purification of the earth, Indra said to him, Puruṣottama, "Descend with a portion of yourself," and Hari replied to him, "So be it."
t.1.58.50: He who bears the discus and the mace in his hands, clad in yellow garments and dark in splendor, the lotus-naveled one, slayer of the enemies of the gods, whose eyes are wide, lovely and gracefully curved.
